title: Once It Was Done: Participle Clauses and Essay Style

sections.content: You know the past participle (*hablado*, *comido*) from A2 Unit 1 and irregular ones such as *hecho*, *escrito* and *abierto* from B2 Unit 20. A participle can also open a clause on its own and say what had been done before the main action: *Terminada la reunión, salimos* means "Once the meeting was over, we left." The noun comes after the participle, and the participle agrees with it like an adjective. The noun is the thing that was done, so the meaning is passive: "the meeting having been finished".

sections.title: Participle clauses
rows: Once the meeting was over, we left.
Terminados los exámenes, los estudiantes salieron.
Once the exams were over, the students left.
Una vez leída la carta, la guardó.
Once the letter was read, he put it away.
Hecho el trabajo, nos fuimos a casa.
The work done, we went home.
Once the letters were written, we sent them.

sections.content: Always match the participle with its noun: *terminada la reunión*, *terminado el trabajo*, *terminados los exámenes*, *escritas las cartas*. *Una vez* before the clause makes the "once" meaning clearer. When the subject of both parts is the same, you can also use *después de* from A2 Unit 4 with an infinitive: *Después de terminar, salimos*; the participle clause is best when the noun is something different from the person who acts.

sections.title: Essay style
sections.content: In a formal essay the same idea of compact writing applies to the whole text. Open a paragraph with a sentence that states its point, often a noun phrase: *El aumento de los precios preocupa a muchas familias.* Grant a point, then limit it. Vary short and long sentences, and use a participle clause or a noun instead of a second *y*. Close with *en conclusión*. The example shows these moves.

items.spanish: El aumento de los precios preocupa a muchas familias.
items.english: The rise in prices worries many families.

items.spanish: Si bien es cierto que los salarios han subido, no lo han hecho tanto como los precios.
items.english: It is true that wages have risen, but not as much as prices.

items.spanish: Aprobada la nueva ley, se espera que la situación mejore.
items.english: Once the new law is passed, the situation is expected to improve.

items.spanish: En conclusión, el aumento de los precios exige medidas.
items.english: In conclusion, the rise in prices calls for measures.
